tests.name: Local agent creation, concurrency and delegation
tests.covers: Main, named and delegated agents create idle persistent agents through tools, inheriting conversation permissions and rejecting inactive calls, edits and permission overrides. New and resumed Codex chats receive a session-bound MCP configuration without replacing history. Agent conversations request native subagents disabled even when untracked; resume appends current developer instructions naming the real creation tool. Only local agent tools are preapproved. Stop, delete and access-setting tools work across provider bridges with compact acknowledgements; Main is undeletable but stoppable and configurable. Idle/access guards reject privilege escalation, extra arguments, self-management and late deletion after a caller stops. Child and grandchild creation inherit all three current conversation access levels rather than profile defaults. Confirmed clear archives Main or a named conversation, creates fresh provider context without changing role/workspace/access, survives restart, rejects pending work and late state changes, and rolls back failed saves. Agent profiles save without waiting for provider startup, reuse discovery and expose startup errors. Independent workers retain separate sessions, serialize overlapping workspaces and Full access, stop individually, return delegated results once, preserve permissions, and fail closed on cleanup or restart. Context reads include Main, search bounded visible transcripts with hash and line provenance, exclude private reasoning and hidden metadata, require an active turn and enforce current workspace/access checks on every call. Each agent retains one conversation, legacy chats migrate without losing history, deletion protects Main and pending work, and repeated delegations return only their own results. Every provider can send exact pasted text to Main; nested task requests wait for final results, reject circular chains, preserve request budgets, and cascade Stop without restarting paused conversations. Agent-created children default to Auto; available model discovery exposes supported efforts, and explicit model/effort selection persists and reaches actual turn parameters across provider bridges without changing the parent. Invalid, disabled and unavailable selections create nothing. Jev enable/disable persists across agents, preserves keys and preferences, uses Smart while off and blocks all Jev requests without reading the key; busy agents prevent toggling.

origin.problem: Harness could run only one active session and had no persistent agent delegation.
origin.fix: Coordinate independent controllers with bounded execution, workspace leases and permission-preserving task handoffs.

tests.name: Codex agent creation reaches the sidebar
tests.covers: Installed Codex resumes an old conversation, receives explicit developer instructions, executes the real agent_create MCP against the Harness backend without another approval, persists inherited permissions and renders the new agent from the state event. Local Responses mock only; no paid inference or user data changes. The new agent_models tool dispatches through real Codex MCP before creation, and the created profile defaults to Auto.

origin.problem: A chat claimed to create an agent using the provider's native subagent tool, while no Harness profile existed; MCP discovery alone missed an execution approval block.
origin.fix: Append current Harness instructions on resume and preapprove only the permission-checked local agent tools; verify a real MCP call through the sidebar.

tests.name: Agent UI and delete dialog selection
tests.covers: Agent creation, switching, deletion through the context menu without sidebar delete buttons, pinned Main with the compact + creation button below it, no bottom New agent/Edit controls, and sidebar scrolling; reopening Delete clears stale text selection. Right-click and Shift+F10 menus use Open/Edit/Delete labels with red Delete, stay within the viewport, support arrow/Enter/Escape navigation and focus restoration, target the clicked agent, and respect Main/busy protections. Slash commands /help /compact /clear /stop /agents /settings run locally without routing/model calls. Clear asks for confirmation and resets only the selected conversation; cancel retains the input. Delegate controls are absent; an agent waiting for nested tasks shows Waiting and keeps Stop targeting its conversation. All buttons and nested button labels are unselectable, including dynamic dialogs, while composer text stays selectable. Shared in-app confirmations show clear/close/startup messages, default to cancellation, handle Escape and repeated opens, retain drafts on cancellation and keep cursor styles visible. Typing / shows all commands, name prefixes filter case-insensitively, arrows and active-descendant track selection, Tab only completes, Enter/click dispatch locally, Escape/blur dismiss, unknown prefixes show an empty state, and the menu fits at 840x640 with 150% text. Selecting clear still confirms. Settings save each dropdown and workspace selection immediately, scoped to the selected agent. Failed saves restore saved/default values and do not block later writes. Check edits and removals autosave; incomplete check drafts survive tab changes and block Close, X and Escape until fixed or removed. API providers join the main provider list as expandable rows, preserve key drafts, and retain save/clear key and confirmed removal actions. API and Jev plug buttons toggle enabled state without expanding settings; Jev keeps its key and supports keyboard toggling. Jev appears as a collapsed provider row, expands by click or keyboard, retains key drafts across provider renders, resets on Settings reopen, and reflects configured/unavailable states. Settings About tab owns the app identity, version, diagnostics, logs and update controls; tab switching hides other panels and existing update checks still work. Offscreen screenshots use software rendering for Linux/Xvfb and Windows, with the output directory created before the first capture. All thirteen slash commands are listed. New command pickers search models, supported efforts, access modes and agents, support keyboard selection and Escape, retain target-agent drafts, persist access for agents without conversations, reject unavailable/busy changes, survive queued close events and fit large text. Context distinguishes reported usage from unsupported providers; status displays task/queue/child data safely. Export writes selected-agent Markdown via a mocked save picker, writes nothing on cancel and preserves input on write errors. Startup and UI checks have separate 30-second budgets so cold Chromium startup cannot consume the test budget; timeout errors report the active phase. Local model controls show load state and context, support load/unload and status retry, disable unloading during agent work, and hide for hosted selections. Connection progress appears in the composer footer and provider rows, includes other agents and browser sign-in, disables duplicate connects, and clears after discovery failure or completion. A computed-style audit checks all populated text and controls at every Font Size option, including sidebar/Overview typography, command descriptions, local-model controls and the + icon; the smallest window at 150% keeps the sidebar scrollable and the heading/access controls readable. The agents divider supports pointer capture, Escape cancellation, arrow/Home/End keys and reset, persists its width across reloads, and clamps to leave conversation room while retaining the preferred width. Dialogs support corner dragging and Alt+arrow resizing with viewport limits; Settings keeps its footer visible and narrowed Overview cards reflow to one column.

origin.problem: Delete dialog retained text selection between deletions.
origin.fix: Clear selection on dialog open/close and prevent selection of button labels.

tests.name: App confirmation replies and cancellation
tests.covers: Confirmation replies require a matching pending id and an explicit boolean. Window close, renderer crash and reload cancel pending operations; unavailable windows never approve.

origin.problem: Native confirmations interrupted the Harness UI and obscured the pointer.
origin.fix: Use styled in-app dialogs over a sender-validated request/reply bridge; cancel requests when their window disappears.

tests.name: Conversation export and compaction records
tests.covers: Markdown export preserves visible messages, plans and Unicode while omitting attachments, pending messages, internal/wiki-maintenance messages, tool arguments and private reasoning. Successful owned Codex and Claude compactions record timestamps; ignored compaction events do not.

origin.problem: Context and export slash commands need provider compaction timestamps and a text-only conversation export.
origin.fix: Record successful compactions and export only visible messages/plans, with regression coverage.

tests.name: Local model lifecycle and context sizing
tests.covers: LM Studio, Ollama and llama.cpp router status, automatic load, unload, actual context limits, context growth, shared-provider serialization, cancellation, hosted-provider fallback and safe load failures. Existing conversations resume with the prepared context before sending. No live inference or downloaded model changes. Structured local inference uses schema-enabled chat completions, preserves runtime model IDs, images, usage and context growth/retry, rejects malformed/truncated responses, holds the provider lock through inference, respects Stop and leaves hosted inference unchanged.

origin.problem: LM Studio rejected a 16.5k prompt because the model was loaded with 8k context; Harness had no model load status or unload controls.
origin.fix: Discover supported native management APIs, coordinate local loads and forward the verified context to Codex, with explicit load/unload controls.

tests.name: Provider connection progress
tests.covers: Startup provider checks, overlapping requests, failures, and browser sign-in success, cancellation, browser-launch failure and disconnect all retain or clear transient progress correctly. No real provider calls.

origin.problem: Provider connection and browser sign-in had no shared progress indicator.
origin.fix: Expose transient per-provider connection state to the footer and Settings, retaining overlapping operations until completion.

tests.name: Hub chat and automatic delegation
tests.covers: Pinned chat model; Hub-only dynamic mid-tier selection using identical Jev/Smart policy and benchmark evidence across arbitrary Codex, Claude-only, Cursor-only and custom-provider models; measured capability extremes are excluded per model without bias from duplicate provider/effort rows, ties and sparse evidence retain usable choices, unknown measurements remain eligible, configurable effort is limited to Low/Medium while fixed/default-effort models stay eligible, pins persist without repeated routing and Auto/manual selection labels retain their origin, legacy pins are reselected, worker catalogs stay unchanged, manual choices work, invalid/high efforts and disabled/rate-limited candidates are rejected, Jev failure falls back to Smart and Stop discards late selections; tool-free inference for all providers, automatic worker creation with Auto and inherited access, attachments, result return through Hub pins despite stale queued/local composer models, persisted effective Hub mode, single Hub dispatch path avoiding manual pins including legacy previous-worker references, explicit worker selection retained, Jev/Smart review routing receives available Claude and local candidates with normal worker effort levels, follow-up reuse, responsive Hub during worker execution, protected identity, rejected escalation, invalid tools, late Stop results, persistent context summaries and retained history. Requested review workspace reaches the worker router; different workspaces require Full access, denied handoffs create nothing, and existing agents are not moved. Auto pins recover from disconnected providers, removed models and usage limits through the same eligible mid-tier policy; Claude-to-OpenAI switching preserves history, persists the replacement and reuses it. Manual pins are never silently replaced. LM Studio-only switching retains history, persists and reuses provider-default effort, skips classification for a sole eligible model, and rejects disabled/limited local models. Jev and Smart both accept fixed-effort candidates; local inference prepares the model and preserves its context configuration without inventing an effort level. Hub uses local structured inference instead of the Responses backend, and malformed replies cannot become agent actions. Typed Hub actions bind tool names to object arguments, preserve Windows/UNC paths, quotes, Unicode and pasted newlines without nested JSON parsing, remove optional nulls while retaining Auto and inherited permissions, and reject legacy strings, arrays, unknown fields, missing required values and invalid types/enums before side effects. Original Hub requests survive misleading notes, saved delegation, result delivery and intervening chat; exact original text drives routing and worker input. New requests reset prior task identity while same-request continuations retain it. Completion checks reject summaries instead of reviews, preserve original scope/images for bounded follow-ups, fail closed on malformed checks and cancelled/failed workers, and mark truncated requests/reports unverified without retries.

origin.problem: The permanent agent mixed chat with execution and retained the task model.
origin.fix: Give Hub a pinned, isolated chat model and dispatch execution through existing agent controls.

tests.name: Worker routing difficulty and effort
tests.covers: Jev and Smart share one difficulty and task-kind contract. Difficulty alone controls effort independently of kind, risk, uncertainty, confidence or unrelated workspace signals. Low/Medium retain adequate models; High/Xhigh choose the strongest measured model across all offered providers within the effort cap. Fixed-effort models, missing benchmarks, current-task continuity and stale sameTask flags remain covered. Raw classifier picks survive policy adjustments. The four-prompt live evaluation fixture records misses and failures without dispatching workers. All structured inference paths validate full JSON and schema, retry malformed replies at most once within a shared deadline, preserve usage, redact model text from errors and honor Stop/limits without retrying. These regressions are offline and use no paid calls.

origin.problem: Confidence alone promoted a bounded explanation to the strongest model while difficult concurrent queue repair stayed at Medium effort.
origin.fix: Classify task difficulty explicitly and share difficulty-based capability/effort selection across Jev and Smart without hardcoded models.
